title: Seoul Has the World's 'Coolest' Neighborhood
paragraphs: Some places are all about the sights. Others are more about the feeling — things like lively streets, cozy cafes and cute little shops that make you want to slow down and stay a little longer.

Those are the types of places Time Out looked for in its latest list of the world's "coolest" neighborhoods. The travel magazine chose 40 areas around the world, based on things like food, culture, nightlife and local atmosphere.

Jongno 3-ga — pronounced sam-ga — in Seoul, South Korea, took the top place. The area mixes old and new, with old Korean houses, modern cafes, little food stalls, small craft shops and lots of late-night bars all packed into its narrow streets. And this isn't its first time on the Time Out "cool" list — Jongno 3-ga also came third in 2021.

Second place went to the L'Ocean area in Morocco's capital, Rabat. In this beachy neighborhood by the Atlantic, visitors can find interesting street art, lively cafes, good Moroccan food and friendly people.

Next on the list was Neos Kosmos in Athens, Greece. Once a quiet, working-class neighborhood, it has changed a lot in recent years, with new art spaces, bars and restaurants. But even with these changes, it still feels very local.
Japan did pretty well too, with two neighborhoods in the top 10.
Kitakagaya in Osaka came sixth. The area was once known for shipbuilding, but many of its old factories have now become art spaces and restaurants, with their walls covered in street art.
And Tokyo's Koenji came eighth. With its vintage clothing stores, record shops, small bars and long punk music history, it certainly sounds cool!
So if you find yourself in one of these places, do yourself a favor: put away the guidebook, get a coffee and see where the streets take you!
